subject: FinBank security questionnaire: hosted API — data control & retention Q&A
messages:
From: Dana Li <dana.li@finbank.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinBank Security Team <security@finbank.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Security questionnaire — hosted API data residency/retention

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this. Our information security team has a short set of follow-ups specific to Redwood's hosted API:
1) Where does customer input (API requests and generated outputs) reside physically/by default (region/datacenter)?
2) What are default retention windows for request logs, KV/prefix caches, and monitoring/tracing artifacts?
3) How do you handle deletion requests — what is the end-to-end timeline and verification?
4) Are customer inputs used to train/finetune models for hosted customers?
5) Are backups/snapshots kept in separate regions; what is retention and encryption model?

Attached is our standard questionnaire — we've highlighted the residency & deletion bits. Can you provide concise answers suitable for our audit?

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Li
Lead, Vendor Security — FinBank
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Li <dana.li@finbank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-18T10:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire — hosted API data residency/retention

Dana — thanks for the questions. High level answers below; attaching a compact CSV that shows per-region residency defaults and a redacted SOC2 for your records. Vivek and Priyom are looped for technical details and export/delete steps.

1) Residency: Default hosted API tenancy is region-specific. For customers in the US we store request payloads (transient) and logs in US regions (multi-AZ within the selected cloud region). EU customers can elect EU-only residency; by default EU customers are routed to eu-central or equivalently configured region. See attached data_residency_table.csv for exact region mappings.

2) Retention: Default retention windows (hosted API): request logs (14 days), detailed traces (30 days), aggregated telemetry (13 months), KV/prefix cache (soft-cache evictions: typically 48–72 hours; persistent cache entries for feature store customers: configurable up to 90 days). We can provide shorter retention on request via DPA addendum.

3) Deletion: For hosted API, customers can request deletion via the customer portal or by raising a support ticket referencing their account id. Standard hosted-data deletion timeline: initial acknowledgement within 24 hours, deletion of request logs/primary data within 72 hours, purging of ephemeral caches within 7 days, removal from live backups within the next backup cycle (up to 30 days). We document final completion and provide a deletion manifest.

4) Training use: Redwood does NOT use hosted-customer input or generated output to train or fine-tune public models. We may use aggregated, anonymized telemetry for product improvement; we never incorporate account-specific data back into model weights for hosted customers without explicit written consent.

5) Backups/encryption: Backups and snapshots are encrypted at rest using cloud KMS keys. Cross-region copies are disabled by default for customers who select single-region residency; we do maintain multi-AZ replicas within the selected region for HA. For customers requiring customer-managed keys or HSM, we offer Private deployment or Dedicated with KMS integration.

Attachments: data_residency_table.csv, SOC2_Type2_redacted.pdf

Let me know if you want the formal answers in the exact questionnaire format and we can provide a signed response.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Li <dana.li@finbank.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-18T12:20:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire — hosted API data residency/retention

Dana — adding technical clarifications from infra/security:

- Encryption: All customer data at rest is encrypted using AES-256. KMS keys are managed by Redwood by default; for Private/Dedicated customers we support customer-managed KMS keys (bring-your-own). TLS 1.2+ in transit.

- Deletion mechanics: Deletion triggers two parallel flows — (1) remove references from the serving runtime and cache eviction, (2) flag records for deletion from object-store backups. We maintain an audit trail of deletion events (who requested, ticket id, timestamps).

- Backups & retention: Point-in-time backups are kept for disaster recovery. For hosted customers with single-region residency selected, snapshot replication is constrained to the same geopolitical region. Snapshots are rotated on a 30-day cycle; a deleted item may persist in older snapshots until snapshot expiry. We can provide accelerated snapshot purge under contractual terms for high-risk regulated customers.

- Logs & traces: Sensitive fields are redacted at ingestion by default (PII tokenization rules). Application-level logs containing full payloads follow the 14-day retention above. Longer-term observability data is aggregated and cannot be mapped back to individual requests without additional identifiers.

- Legal hold / litigation: Legal holds may extend retention; we require a formal legal process to request suspension of deletion. We will notify the customer and coordinate with FinBank's legal team if needed.

- Training: To re-iterate, hosted API customer inputs are not used to train Redwood public models. Any customer-requested model training would use explicitly supplied datasets under a separate agreement.

Happy to provide a short technical addendum for your auditors.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Security questionnaire — hosted API data residency/retention

Dana — quick practical notes for FinBank operations team if you want to exercise deletion/export:

- Export: We can produce a JSON/NDJSON export of all request/response pairs for a given account id. Typical turnaround is 48–72 hours after the export request; the export is delivered via a time-limited secure link (S3 presigned URL) or via an encrypted transfer.

- Deletion request process: 1) Open support ticket or use the portal link (shared below) 2) Provide account id and date range 3) We acknowledge (24h) -> scheduled purge (<=72h) -> confirm with deletion manifest.

- Verification: We provide a manifest (hashes and object keys) after deletion; for auditors we can provide redacted logs showing the deletion workflow.

Portal link for DPA/deletion/export requests: https://redwood.example.com/dpa/DBL-8421

Let me know if you want me to open a ticket and start an export for a specific range.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is very helpful. Two follow-ups: (1) please confirm the maximum time a deleted record could remain recoverable due to snapshots (I understand up to 30 days unless special purge is arranged) and (2) we'd like a one-time export for account FIN-87233 covering 2025-11-01 to 2026-02-18. Please provide the secure export link and deletion manifest when complete.

Also, can you confirm in writing that Redwood will not use the exported data for model training? We need this explicitly for our audit trail.

Best,
Dana

Subject: Re: Security questionnaire — hosted API data residency/retention

Dana — confirmed:

- Snapshot exposure window: for standard hosted customers, deleted items may be recoverable from snapshots for up to 30 days (snapshot expiry window). We can arrange an accelerated purge under contract — please let me know if FinBank needs snapshot purge terms in the DPA.

- Export: we've begun the export request for account FIN-87233 (range 2025-11-01 -> 2026-02-18). You will receive a time-limited secure export link (S3 presigned URL) to the security contact on file within 48 hours. The export manifest (finbank_export_manifest.json) will accompany the delivery.

- Training assurance: Redwood will NOT use the exported data or any hosted-customer data for model training or to fine-tune public models unless explicit, written customer consent is given. We will include that assurance in the written DPA response.

Next steps: Priyom will send the export link when ready and Vivek will prepare a short technical addendum for your auditors. If you'd like a signed statement for procurement, I can coordinate legal to add the snapshot purge language to the DPA.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
